standard_prerequisites: Existing1921 general strong-Markov criterion, preserving its arbitrarily-small-scale formulation
CAT(-1) comparison geometry, Busemann functions and metric-Anosov property at author cited granularity
core_obligations: Given the existing1921 regular-pre-Markov criterion, standard CAT(-1) Busemann geometry and metric-Anosov structure, the author must still construct actual good geometric rectangles at every sufficiently smallscale. The proof obtains quantitative linear Busemann bounds, Lipschitz return times and a one-half Holder projection estimate, then refines and shifts finite rectangle families while preserving coverage, disjointness and the pre-Markov intersection constraints. The recursive construction eliminates bad intersections without losing previously good conditions and closes on the compact non-wandering set; transitivity yields irreducibility. This coordinated nonsmooth geometric/regularity construction is one H2 principal result beyond a direct application of the supplied criterion. Individual distance/log bounds and the projective adaptation/statistical consequences are retained without separate counts.
proof_roadmap: Construct good Busemann rectangles, prove return-time/projection regularity, build/refine finite proper families at arbitrary small scales, apply existing general criterion and transitivity. Preserve projective and statistical companion sections at author granularity.
